heroHeadline: China Embassy Note Interrupts Philippine Defense Chief Mid-Speech at Seoul Forum; Teodoro Reads It Aloud On Stage, Calls It 'Coercion, Bullying'
heroSubtitle: Philippine Secretary of National Defense Gilberto Teodoro Jr. was handed a handwritten note from a Chinese embassy military attache while speaking on a 'gray zone' coercion panel at the Seoul Defense Dialogue on September 8, 2026. The note restated Beijing's rejection of the 2016 South China Sea arbitral award as 'illegal, null and void.' Teodoro read it aloud line by line, rebutting each point — 'Of course, because you lost' — and told the forum, 'This is not gray zone anymore, this is actual coercion, bullying and aggression,' saying he would keep the note 'as a memento of how desperate China is.' Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning responded September 9, urging 'certain individuals in the Philippines to stop clout-chasing, stop making trouble and stirring up strife,' and accusing Manila of 'grandstanding and lying.' The exchange follows the PCG's September 4 disclosure that the drilling-capable Chinese survey vessel Haiyang Dizhi Shihao spent 25 days in the Philippine EEZ without a permit, and the DFA's tally of 296 diplomatic protests against China since 2022.
